articles.title: Milsinho anuncia lançamento de projeto novo da Toque Dez | G1
articles.standfirst: Banda foi uma das atrações a desfilar no Circuito Maneca Ferreira nesta quinta-feira (19), primeira noite da festa.
articles.summary: Banda foi uma das atrações a desfilar no Circuito Maneca Ferreira nesta quinta-feira (19), primeira noite da festa.
articles.body:
Milsinho, vocalista da banda Toque Dez, na Micareta de Feira de Santana 2026 — Foto: João Souza/g1

O arrocha tem conquistado cada vez mais espaço na Micareta de Feira de Santana . A cada ano, Milsinho, vocalista da banda Toque Dez , ganha ainda mais destaque no Circuito Maneca Ferreira, na Avenida Presidente Dutra, principal palco da festa que toma as ruas da segunda maior cidade da Bahia neste feriadão.

Em entrevista ao g1 , nesta quinta-feira (19), o cantor comemorou mais uma participação no evento e destacou o carinho do público feirense.

"Sempre falo: quando eu venho tocar aqui, eu me sinto em casa. Pelo carinho, pelo acolhimento da galera", afirmou.

O artista também adiantou novidades no repertório e contou que a banda pretende lançar um novo projeto em dezembro.

"Estaremos com muito arrocha, muita sofrência. Eu até falei que hoje vai ter repertório novo. A gente quer lançar agora um projeto, acho que dia 2 de dezembro. Então, hoje vai ser um show espetacular, um show à parte", reforçou.

Após a participação na micareta, na sexta-feira (20), o cantor tem apresentação marcada em Salvador, no projeto "Na Máxima".

A Micareta de Feira segue até o próximo domingo (22 ). Durante os dias de festa, estão previstos desfiles de artistas como Carlinhos Brown, Pedro Sampaio, Xanddy Harmonia, Tony Salles, Psirico, Léo Santana e Pablo.

Nesta primeira noite, além de Toque Dez, os foliões da cidade curtiram os desfiles de Claudia Leitte, Timbalada, Robyssão e muito mais.

articles.title: Robyssão lembra luta por liberdade de expressão no pagodão | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantor celebrou o novo momento do ritmo em entrevista ao g1 nos bastidores da Micareta de Feira de Santana. Artista foi uma das atrações da festa, que se estende até domingo (22), no Circuito Maneca Ferreira.
articles.summary: Cantor celebrou o novo momento do ritmo em entrevista ao g1 nos bastidores da Micareta de Feira de Santana. Artista foi uma das atrações da festa.
articles.body:
Hoje um dos nomes mais experientes do pagodão baiano, Robyssão avalia que nem sempre os representantes do ritmo tiveram liberdade para cantar sobre diversos temas. O ex-vocalista do Balck Style ressalta que foi alvo de muitas críticas no passado por ousar com canções de duplo sentido.

"Eu fui um cara que recebi muitos bombardeios, porque minhas músicas sempre foram irreverentes, músicas de duplo sentido, e eu acho que isso que está acontecendo hoje é uma grande vitória".

A avaliação foi feita em entrevista ao g1 , nos bastidores da Micareta de Feira de Santana , na noite desta quinta-feira (19). Ele foi uma das primeiras atrações a comandar um trio no Circuito Maneca Ferreira, onde a festa segue até domingo (22).

Ao falar com o portal, Robyssão celebrou o novo momento vivido por artistas do gênero. "Tive que tomar muitas porradas para que artistas tivessem liberdade de expressão. (...) Lutei para que artistas pudessem abordar qualquer assunto, qualquer tema, sejam problemas sociais, sejam problemas relacionados a questões sexuais. Hoje, as pessoas têm liberdade, os artistas têm liberdade e podem abordar qualquer assunto, e isso é bom", destacou.

Robyssão foi uma das atrações da Micareta de Feira 2026 — Foto: João Souza/g1

Conhecido entre os fãs mais jovens como Tio Roby, o cantor também comentou sobre a surpresa de conquistar o público da geração Z, mesmo tendo construído a carreira em outra época.

"A coisa mais difícil que existe é você conquistar a geração Z, é quase que impossível. Eu sou das antigas, então é algo muito raro o que está acontecendo comigo: a geração Z consumir minhas músicas, frequentar meus shows e ainda me denominar como tio, tio Roby, né? Aí, daqui a um tempo, o que vai ser? Avô Roby, vovô Roby", brincou.

Em fevereiro de 2026, durante o Carnaval, Robyssão viralizou nas redes sociais ao comentar que vários artistas se envolveram em brigas e polêmicas durante a festa, enquanto ele não havia participado de nenhuma confusão.

Na entrevista, o cantor refletiu sobre essa postura. "Eu gosto de passar mensagens motivacionais, porque as pessoas andam às vezes perdidas, confusas, sobretudo os mais jovens. E a última mensagem que eu estou passando para essa turma mais jovem é para não desistir dos seus sonhos. Se você tem um sonho, lute. Não se arrependa, vá em frente. Se não der certo, pelo menos deu errado", aconselhou, em tom de brincadeira.

Carnaval fora de época recebe diversos artistas

Além de Robyssão, Claudia Leitte, Timbalada e Toque Dez estiveram entre as atrações desta primeira noite. A programação principal, até domingo, tem ainda diversos nomes como Pedro Sampaio e Michelle Andrade. Na segunda-feira (23), mais uma vez, Feira de Santana será palco para o "Arrastão", comandado por Thiago Aquino.

articles.title: Alonso: "Lo que recuerdo del Dakar es el dolor de cabeza, no puedes pestañear en 4 ó 5 horas"
articles.standfirst: Fernando explica en profundidad por qué ha dado el sí a la prueba más dura del motor y descarta la posibilidad de ganar el Rally... con la boca pequeña
articles.summary: Fernando explica en profundidad por qué ha dado el sí a la prueba más dura del motor y descarta la posibilidad de ganar el Rally... con la boca pequeña
articles.body: La rueda de prensa de Fernando Alonso en Las Vegas ha sido casi monográfica del Dakar, tras el reciente anuncio de que lo afrontará con Aston Martin este enero, siete años después de su primera participación. Como era natural, después de dos respuestas negativas en anteriores comparecencias respecto a participar el al clásico del desierto mientras se sigue en la F1, le recordaron sus propias palabras. "No creo que sea posible, es casi imposible", dijo en Singapur. "Sí, bueno, sigo pensando lo mismo; no he cambiado de opinión. Creo que el Dakar de 2027 será un desafío mucho mayor de lo que fue para mí en 2020. En aquel entonces tuve seis meses de preparación: fui a probar a distintos países, como Qatar, Namibia, Marruecos y Polonia; fue un programa bastante extenso. Además, creo que participé en dos rallies en Arabia Saudí. Ahora sólo tendré dos días en Marruecos y luego, ¡allá vamos! Es un periodo bastante corto, pero al final decidimos, junto con el equipo, Prodrive y Aston, que sigue siendo una buena experiencia para todas las partes, especialmente para mí, porque no es ningún secreto que algún día quiero ganar el Dakar. Este año no será posible, pero lo considero una inversión de cara al futuro: sumar más kilómetros y conocer mejor la disciplina", argumentaba el asturiano. Lo que quiere dejar claro es que sus expectativas son relativamente modestas y se lo toma como un aprendizaje para el futuro. "Creo que tiene sentido, es un mes en el que no hay mucha actividad en la F1. Es un coche divertido de conducir y resulta una experiencia gratificante, tanto en el plano profesional como en el personal. Como ya he dicho, es uno de los mayores retos, precisamente por la falta de preparación; aun así, intentaré realizar pruebas durante la primera semana y, con suerte, competir en la segunda", dice sobre el plan. Habla de la preparación como factor crucial y sus explicaciones sobre su experiencia de 2020 son más que interesantes. "Los pilotos que compiten allí llevan toda la vida haciéndolo. Se han criado en el mundo del automovilismo dentro de los rallies y con este tipo de vehículos; saben interpretar los distintos terrenos, los matices, las variaciones en la luz...", desmenuzaba. "En el Dakar hay muchísimos aspectos que son totalmente diferentes. En la F1, en un circuito, se trata de repetir lo mismo una vuelta tras otra, tratando de perfeccionar el estilo de conducción. En los rallies, todo consiste en improvisar; improvisar constantemente, porque no sabes qué va a pasar en el siguiente metro. Una de mis fortalezas siempre ha sido la capacidad de adaptarme rápidamente a las situaciones y a los cambios, pero esto es otro nivel. Recuerdo que, durante mis primeras jornadas de pruebas en el Dakar, terminaba por la noche con dolor de cabeza", rememoraba. "Creo que se debe al nivel de concentración que requiere, algo a lo que no estoy acostumbrado. No puedes ni parpadear durante cuatro o cinco horas. En cambio, aquí [en la Fórmula 1], ajustamos parámetros en el volante, nos comunicamos por radio, observamos las pantallas y seguimos la carrera; al fin y al cabo, te mantienes en un entorno reducido, vuelta tras vuelta", compara entre ambas disciplinas. "En el Dakar, te adentras en lo desconocido. Cada metro es nuevo. Dada mi trayectoria, el desafío es mayor que para alguien que no se ha formado en esta disciplina", añadía. Sobre sus opciones de éxito, prefiere la cautela y se remite a la experiencia de uno de sus compañeros en Aston Martin para 2027. "No sé... creo que he demostrado ser competitivo, pero, como mencioné, en su momento conté con unos seis meses de preparación y varios miles de kilómetros de pruebas previos, algo de lo que ahora no dispongo. Mi compañero de equipo actual, Sébastien Loeb, es probablemente el mejor piloto de rallies de la historia. Ha participado en el Dakar nueve o diez veces y aún no ha logrado la victoria. Soy consciente de la dificultad, pero precisamente por eso resulta tan atractivo: es un desafío enorme. Para Fernando lo crucial es esa dificultad que entraña asumir el desafío. "Por eso es interesante y por eso quiero intentar ganarlo algún día. Sí. No, eso no ha cambiado. El Dakar siempre ha estado presente en mis planes. También Le Mans y las 500 Millas de Indianápolis...", recalca. "Me encanta competir. Me apasiona pilotar coches de carreras: pisas el acelerador y sientes la potencia; pisas el freno y experimentas la deceleración. Son sensaciones que, hoy en día, echamos de menos en la Fórmula 1, por eso pensaba en todo esto. Por supuesto, al continuar en la Fórmula 1 esa será siempre mi prioridad y resulta complicado compaginarla con otros programas. El Dakar, al celebrarse en enero, encaja algo mejor, aunque también han tenido que darse ciertas circunstancias", especificaba. Fernando explicaba de dónde salió este proyecto y cómo se concretó. "Creo que esto fue allá por julio. David Richards vino, probablemente durante la carrera en Silverstone, y ya tuvimos esa conversación; aunque, en aquel momento, ni siquiera se planteó la participación. Él simplemente estaba allí con Prodrive. Así que le dije: 'No lo sé, David; no sé qué pasará el año que viene'". Estaba claro que en ese momento la retirada de la F1 seguía siendo una posibilidad. "Al final, todo encajó rápidamente; estoy contento y preparado para aprender tanto como sea posible", añadía Alonso sobre lo que viene. Con tan corta preparación y ante la magnitud del reto, le cuestionaron sobre si sel Dakar supone ponerse en peligro. No se dice la palabra accidente, pero se sobreentiende. "No, en absoluto", zanjaba. ¿Y qué dijeron en Aston Martin?: "Estuvieron encantados. Saben que necesito conducir algo... Piloto todas las semanas, varias cosas. A veces, como ya he comentado en alguna ocasión, piloto coches de Fórmula 1. que ni siquiera son Aston Martin ni nada por el estilo, y en este caso, al menos, se trata de la misma marca y los mismos colores". Fernando descarta que no tenga el control a bordo de un coche del Dakar. "Tengo el control total del coche. Lo que no controlo del todo es la velocidad a la que me acerco a los peligros. Por ejemplo, cuando voy con un copiloto excelente como Marc Coma, a veces, tras recorrer quizá 10 kilómetros a fondo en medio de la nada, él divisa a lo lejos un poco de vegetación o algo verde; siempre me avisa: 'Si ves algo verde, prepárate, que vienen baches'", decía con tono humorístico. "Así que voy aprendiendo estas cosas sobre la marcha, gracias a su experiencia. Supongo que, para otros pilotos, todo esto es algo automático porque ya han pasado por situaciones similares. Por tanto, estoy en un proceso de aprendizaje acelerado, justo en plena carrera. Pero, como piloto, me resulta fascinante", aseguraba. Si en su cabeza sigue la idea de completar la Triple Corona y volver a Indianápolis, Fernando duda. Pues no lo sé. "Van a cambiar los coches pronto. Algún día... bueno, creo que el año que viene. Llega un coche nuevo. Así que, no sé... quizá algún día me lo plantee. No está en mis planes a corto plazo, no lo tengo en mente ahora mismo, pero no puedo decir que sea un 'no' rotundo", deslizaba En cuanto al rumor de hacer también las 24 Horas de Le Mans en 2027, Fernando contestaba: "No, por el momento sólo la F1 y el Dakar". Es un no, pero no lo niega definitivamente tampoco.

articles.title: Paul Nicholls breaks record for National Hunt wins after surpassing Martin Pipe’s all-time tally with Warwick triumph
articles.summary: Ditcheat handler Paul Nicholls became the winning-most trainer in British National Hunt history, surpassing the great Martin Pipe's total of 3,390 when Knappers Hill crossed the line in front at Lingfield, donning the colours of Paul Barber
articles.body:
The 14-time champion eclipsed Pipe's record of 3,930 wins at Warwick on Thursday after Knappers Hill toughed out victory in the Denis O'Connell Memorial Veterans' Handicap Chase under Sam Twiston-Davies, carrying the colours of the trainer's long-time friend and mentor Paul Barber.

Nicholls, who has been training at Manor Farm Stables in Somerset since 1991 after first renting the yard from Barber, was thrilled to etch his name into the history of a sport in which he has long been a master of his craft.

"I never thought when I started training we'd ever train that many winners, but it's a nice milestone," said Nicholls, whose tally includes famous victories by all-time great horses such as Kauto Star, Big Buck's and Denman.

"We're not far off 4,000 winners that have been sent out across all codes, but they'll get beaten again in the future because records are always there to be broken.

"You'd probably have thought Martin would never have been beaten. What a fantastic trainer he was.

"Hopefully we can head on with the British winners and end up with getting near the 4,000. It's exciting."

Nicholls added: "As you keep racking up these winners, you're getting closer and closer.

"A year ago, I wouldn't have known the exact number, but then, of course, everyone fills you in and now you know.

"It's just a target, isn't it? Dan [Skelton] is targeting beating Martin's record of winners in a season. We all like beating records.

"It's nice to be the winning-most National Hunt trainer in Britain, even if it's not forever, it's nice to do that. It just reflects well on the whole team at Ditcheat and the whole set-up really and what we've done here."

Olveston has more meaning than most for Nicholls as it is not only the village where he was raised, but it is also the name of his first winner.

What made it even more special was his father Brian was a part-owner and family has been a running theme throughout his 35 years at Manor Farm, with daughters Megan and Olive and nephew Harry Derham all playing their part along the way.

He added: "I remember my first winner. It was December 20, 1991 at Hereford. Dad was involved in Olveston with some mates. It was brilliant.

"Megan's had a lot of winners, Olive has, Harry Derham was here and dad's still here every day.

"I've been incredibly lucky, I've had some great people around me, some fantastic horses. We keep trying to work hard and do the best we can.

"Paul Barber was a big part of my life and lots of people along the way. Lots of people have gone on to be good jockeys, lots of people have been gone on to be great trainers.

"It's just been a fantastic journey. I pinch myself to think I've been here 35 years now, it just seems like it was yesterday. I don't know where time goes."

As he targets his next landmark, what remaining ambitions does Nicholls have for a trainer who has won it all?

"Keep training winners, still loving the game. I love the game. It's just awesome," said Nicholls, who is still one short of Pipe's 15 champion trainer titles.

"I've invested quite heavily in some new facilities this year, I've got some nice young horses and a good team around me. I love it, just training big winners."

articles.title: Paul Nicholls: Breaks Martin Pipe’s all-time National Hunt tally for winners by a British trainer
articles.summary: Paul Nicholls surpasses Martin Pipe to set a new National Hunt record for winners by a British trainer.
articles.body:
Paul Nicholls has surpassed Martin Pipe to set a new National Hunt record for winners by a British trainer.

The 14-time champion claimed his 3,931st win at Warwick on Thursday as Knappers Hill secured victory in the Denis O'Connell Memorial Veterans' Handicap Chase.

Since starting as a trainer in 1991, Nicholls has gone on to look after some legendary horses such as Kauto Star, Big Buck's and Denman.

"I never thought when I started training we'd ever train that many winners, but it's a nice milestone," said the 64-year-old.

"We're not far off 4,000 winners that have been sent out across all codes, but they'll get beaten again in the future because records are always there to be broken.

"You'd probably have thought Martin would never have been beaten. What a fantastic trainer he was.

"Hopefully we can head on with the British winners and end up with getting near the 4,000. It's exciting."

Nicholls' first winner came in December 1991 with Olveston - a horse with the same name as the Gloucestershire village he grew up and was part-time owned by his father.

From there he went from strength to strength, training four Cheltenham Gold Cup winners and had Grand National success with Neptune Collonges in 2012.

"It's nice to be the winning-most National Hunt trainer in Britain, even if it's not forever, it's nice to do that," added the Somerset-based Nicholls.

"It just reflects well on the whole team at Ditcheat and the whole set-up really and what we've done here."

articles.title: Jorge Martín: "No voy a ser el que vaya a tirar a Marc Márquez, no todo vale"
articles.standfirst: No da todo por perdido, aunque es realista
articles.summary: No da todo por perdido, aunque es realista
articles.body: Jorge Martín es más que consciente de sus pocas opciones de mantener vivo el Mundial de MotoGP 2026 en el Gran Premio de Portugal, en Portimao. Eso sí, advierte que está ya casi a tope físicamente, sin molestias en el radio de la muñeca derecha. Considera un orgullo haber peleado, y pelear, con Marc Márquez. "Posible es, eso está claro, pero no está en mi control. Mi control sólo está en intentar ganar las cuatro carreras que quedan y es lo que voy a intentar. Estar muy concentrado en hacer bien lo que sé hacer, que es ir en moto, en pilotar. Está claro que no puedo controlar lo que él haga, así que todo puede pasar. Estoy en MotoGP y en el deporte todo puede pasar, pero no está en mi control. Es muy difícil, pero posibilidades sí que hay". "Si no estoy al 100%, estoy muy cerca. Tengo un poco de dolor, pero creo que la moto no me va a condicionar para nada, así que estoy preparado. Creo que he hecho un gran trabajo esta semana; me ha venido muy bien descansar, con ganas de ver mi potencial al 100%, de volver a coger la pila que está funcionando muy bien. Y aparte, en dos pistas donde ganaron el año pasado, creo que podemos hacer un buen trabajo". "Es verdad que ha sido inoportuna, pero mirando un poco con perspectiva, Marc ha tenido una lesión, Marco ha tenido una lesión y yo he tenido una lesión; al final hemos empatado. Obviamente, es una pena, pero mirando con perspectiva, a principio de año no me podía poner el mono y estoy a falta de dos carreras peleando por ganar un Mundial. Estar aquí ya es una victoria y voy a intentar todo lo que pueda para alargarlo. Pero yo no voy a ser el que vaya a tirar a Marc y luego intentar ganar porque, para mí, no todo vale, vale estar concentrado, intentar ganar el sábado, intentar ganar el domingo y luego, si algo pasa y me llega la oportunidad ahí estaré para cogerla". "Me da igual. Está claro que es mejor tercero que cuarto y segundo que tercero, pero el valor de un subcampeonato o un tercero para mí es el mismo; al final es no ser campeón. No es algo que esté en mi mente; quizá otros pilotos lo tienen en mente, pero no es mi caso. Yo intentaré pelear por ganar por mí, por acabar bien con Aprilia, para acabar bien estos dos años que no han sido fáciles y al final he conseguido rehacerme como piloto. Lo que tenga que ser, pues será". "Yo creo que todo el año he ido un poco con la mochila de no haber corrido el año pasado y quizá en Austria empecé a encontrarme mejor. Fue cuando ya por fin me encontraba ahí para pelear y estaba en la pelea. Está claro que es una pena, pero en Australia fallé y eso ha provocado que ahora las opciones del mundial sean mucho más lejanas. De todas formas, me quedo con estar peleando con uno de los mejores pilotos de la historia, si no el mejor, a su mejor nivel; él mismo lo ha dicho, y estoy aquí peleando contra él. Eso al final me demuestra mi valor y creo que es un privilegio y estoy muy orgulloso de lo que estoy consiguiendo". "Al final, he pasado mucho, pero Marc también ha pasado mucho. Creo que cada persona o cada piloto tiene su mochila. Al ser más conocidos o por la fama, se sabe todo de nosotros, pero creo que todo el mundo tiene su lucha personal. Esta ha sido la mía y está claro que si puedo ayudar a gente a que siga luchando y ayudar a gente a que salga de un momento duro, pues yo encantado". "Si en parte lo hago, también es por esto, por ayudar a gente que me escribe, que está con enfermedades crónicas, que lo está pasando muy mal y aún por verme correr, por ver que después con el brazo roto sigo luchando y eso al final le da mucho valor a mi trabajo".

articles.title: FIA announce introduction of full-time F1 stewards from 2027 ahead of Las Vegas Grand Prix
articles.summary: Formula 1's governing body, the FIA, has revealed full-time stewards will be used for the first time from next year; watch the Las Vegas GP weekend on Sky Sports F1, with Friday's practice sessions at 12.30am and 4pm
articles.body:
The use of full-time stewards has been a consistent talking point in F1 as different stewards, who adjudicate all racing and technical matters on a race weekend, are used at each event over the season.

There has been an argument that this can lead to inconsistencies in decision-making when it comes to imposing penalties, or the severity of a penalty.

But the FIA announced on Thursday, ahead of this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix, they will begin to recruit full-time stewards with a phased introduction from next year with the aim of establishing 12-15 full-time stewards over the coming years.

Currently, there are four stewards drawn from a large FIA pool of officials and one of those is a former racing driver. The new structure will continue to use the knowledge of driver stewards at each event and the FIA say full-time stewards will "allow for deeper implementation of best practice and greater consistency in decision-making".

The news comes a month after the opening of the FIA Remote Operations Centre at Biggin Hill in the UK, following a reorganisation of Race Control in 2022 after the controversial 2021 season which saw Max Verstappen overtake Lewis Hamilton on the last lap of the season-ending Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

"This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to delivering the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport," said FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem.

"The recruitment of full-time stewards is a significant step in our longstanding mission of building a dedicated officiating ecosystem in the FIA Formula One World Championship, it is also an investment in the future of our sport.

"Following the milestone opening of the new FIA Remote Operations Centre and strengthening of officiating development through initiatives such as the FIA High Performance Programme, this development will help to build greater expertise and continuity within our stewarding structure, strengthening our ability to review and improve regulations, support the development of future officials and ensure the highest standards of consistent officiating across all our championships."

articles.title: F1 to introduce full-time race stewards from 2027
articles.summary: Formula 1's governing body the FIA is to introduce permanent race stewards from the 2027 season.
articles.body:
Formula 1's governing body the FIA is to introduce permanent race stewards from the 2027 season.

The move follows consistent calls from grand prix drivers for the change because of criticisms of inconsistency of decisions regarding penalties for on-track incidents.

The FIA said in a statement that it would begin recruiting permanent stewards, and was planning a "phased introduction" during the 2027 season.

The FIA statement added: "The introduction of dedicated full-time stewards to the FIA's flagship championship will provide continuity and expertise within the stewarding structure, further advancing the FIA's commitment to fairness through the ongoing review and continuous improvement of sporting regulations and stewarding guidelines.

"It will also allow for deeper implementation of best practice and greater consistency in decision-making."

It said that the use of driver stewards, usually an ex-F1 driver, would continue, "recognising the invaluable expertise they bring".

The plan is for "a small number" of full-time stewards to be recruited during 2027 and the group to be expanded from 2028.

"Existing FIA stewards will continue to play a vital role, contributing their experience within a mixed roster of full-time and part-time stewards for the foreseeable future," the statement said.

In reality, the move is not a major step on from the current situation, where a small number of stewards are rotated around races.

Each grand prix has a group of four stewards, one of which is an ex-driver.

Current drivers have often referenced the fact that they had repeatedly complained during briefings with FIA officials that rulings on driver standards and racing errors were not applied on a consistent basis.

Last year, Williams driver Carlos Sainz, a director of drivers' body the Grand Prix Drivers' Association, said: "F1 and the FIA all agree that [permanent stewards] should be the way forward, where at least two of the three stewards are permanent and we have one rotational for teaching purposes."

The decision follows the opening of an FIA race operations centre at F1's Biggin Hill headquarters in south London.

The FIA has in recent years received increased income from F1 - which provides the majority of its funding - on the basis that this would be applied to improving officialdom and rule-making.

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said: "This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to delivering the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport.

"The recruitment of full-time stewards is a significant step in our longstanding mission of building a dedicated officiating ecosystem in the FIA Formula 1 World Championship, it is also an investment in the future of our sport."

articles.title: Black Friday de viagens: 3 dicas para aproveitar o interior de SP  | G1
articles.standfirst: Com atrações de natureza, passeios ao ar livre e resorts com piscinas aquecidas, Atibaia é alternativa para quem quer planejar uma viagem com descontos
articles.summary: Com atrações de natureza, passeios ao ar livre e resorts com piscinas aquecidas, Atibaia é alternativa para quem quer planejar uma viagem com descontos
articles.body:
A Black Friday também pode ser uma oportunidade para tirar aquela viagem em família do papel. Em vez de procurar apenas ofertas de produtos, quem deseja aproveitar o período para descansar pode encontrar boas oportunidades em hotéis, resorts e destinos turísticos do interior de São Paulo.

Uma das opções é Atibaia, cidade que reúne atrações naturais, parques, gastronomia e hospedagens com estrutura de lazer para diferentes idades. Localizada no interior paulista, a cidade é uma alternativa para quem busca alguns dias de descanso sem precisar fazer uma viagem longa.

Entre os destaques está o Atibaia Residence Hotel & Resort, que oferece sistema all-inclusive, piscinas aquecidas e programação de recreação para crianças. A cidade também tem passeios que podem complementar a hospedagem, especialmente para quem gosta de natureza e atividades ao ar livre.

A primeira dica é pesquisar com antecedência e comparar as condições das ofertas. Durante a Black Friday, hotéis e resorts costumam apresentar tarifas promocionais para períodos específicos, o que permite organizar viagens futuras e aproveitar descontos.

Em Atibaia, o Atibaia Residence Hotel & Resort anunciou sua campanha Black Friday 2026/2027. A promoção será realizada entre os dias 27 e 29 de novembro, exclusivamente pelo site oficial do empreendimento.

De acordo com as regras divulgadas pelo resort, os descontos serão de 30% e 50%, dependendo do período de hospedagem e da disponibilidade das tarifas promocionais. O pagamento poderá ser parcelado em até seis vezes sem juros no cartão de crédito.

Antes de fechar a reserva, vale conferir as datas disponíveis, o número mínimo de diárias e as condições para alterações e cancelamentos.

Para quem viaja com crianças, escolher uma hospedagem que ofereça atividades para diferentes idades pode fazer a diferença. Assim, os adultos conseguem descansar enquanto os pequenos aproveitam a programação de recreação.

O Atibaia Residence Hotel & Resort trabalha com sistema all-inclusive, que inclui refeições, petiscos e bebidas durante a estadia, conforme os horários e as condições do serviço.

A estrutura também conta com piscinas aquecidas, áreas verdes, espaços de lazer e atividades esportivas. Entre as opções de aventura estão arvorismo e tirolesa.

Outro destaque é a programação infantil, que pode incluir gincanas, caça ao tesouro, oficinas de criatividade, brincadeiras na piscina e atividades acompanhadas por recreadores. As opções variam de acordo com o pacote e o período da hospedagem.

Um dos cartões-postais de Atibaia é a Pedra Grande, formação natural. O local é conhecido pelas paisagens panorâmicas e pela prática de voo livre, além de atrair visitantes interessados em trilhas e contato com a natureza.

O monumento natural oferece uma vista ampla da região e, em dias de boa visibilidade, permite observar diversas cidades do entorno.

Outra alternativa é conhecer o Parque Municipal Edmundo Zanoni, um dos espaços de lazer mais tradicionais da cidade. O parque reúne áreas verdes, lago com pedalinho, playground, jardim japonês e o Museu de História Natural. É uma opção para passear com crianças, caminhar e aproveitar um momento mais tranquilo durante a viagem.

Importante lembrar que a cidade integra o Circuito das Frutas e tem tradição na produção de morangos e flores. A região conta ainda com propriedades rurais, fazendas, alambiques artesanais e restaurantes que valorizam ingredientes e receitas locais.

Dependendo da época da visita, é possível encontrar experiências ligadas à produção agrícola e ao turismo rural, uma alternativa para quem deseja sair um pouco do roteiro tradicional.

articles.title: Could IndyCar return to Kansas? Series testing the waters on oval
articles.summary: IndyCar drivers Pato O'Ward and Will Power are testing at Kansas Speedway, fueling rumors of a potential return in 2027.
articles.body:
Four weeks after IndyCar announced its 2027 schedule , the series is testing the waters at a track not on the schedule. On Friday, Arrow McLaren's Pato O'Ward and Andretti Global's Will Power will drive on the Kansas Speedway oval in Kansas City, Kansas.

Per an IndyCar spokesperson, it is an aerodynamic validation test as the series "gathers information and data in the event an opportunity arises to race on the 1.5-mile oval in the future." IndyCar declined to reveal whether the future could be as soon as 2027.

IndyCar hasn't raced at Kansas Speedway since 2010. The series raced at the track for a decade after it opened in 2001, but hasn't returned since.

IndyCar hasn't visited Kansas Speedway in any capacity since the introduction of its current Dallara DW12 chassis in 2012, thus the need to test the current aerodynamic package at the track. It's worth noting that 2027 is slated to be the final year of the DW12, as Dallara's IR28 will debut in 2028 after it went through a series of validation tests this year. Testing the current car would suggest that IndyCar has interest in racing at the track in 2027.

IndyStar's best photos from the 110th running of the Indianapolis 500

When Nashville Superspeedway was removed from IndyCar's schedule in October, it left the series with four oval tracks (and five races) in 2027. IndyCar president Doug Boles claimed losing Nashville was "something that none of us want to see" and that finding additional ovals was a "big priority" for the series .

"The question really becomes, how can we go into a market where the attendance will make it feel like an event?" Boles asked. "I think that's really important to us to get into that. Where do we have a promoter that doesn't just want us, but is willing to promote alongside us and really be that lead in that community to help drive the attendance is an important piece of that. ... There's a significant number of tracks, like I said, that would have interest. It's just a matter now of finding the right one where we think we can have the most success, where we can create the racing that we're so known for on the ovals."

If IndyCar races at Kansas in 2027, it seems likely that it'd be in tandem with NASCAR, which owns the track. NASCAR has two Cup Series races at Kansas in 2027, with one being in its postseason "The Chase." The other race is slated for Sunday, May 9.

There exists a world where IndyCar holds a race at Kansas the day before the Cup Series race. In March, IndyCar returned to Phoenix Raceway, another NASCAR-owned oval, for a Saturday-Sunday doubleheader. IndyCar and NASCAR will repeat that doubleheader in 2027 , signifying a growing relationship between America's two major motorsports series.

"We wouldn't be opposed to looking at other oval tracks where we could partner together," Boles told IndyStar in March . "The biggest challenge in it is (the) schedule and finding a date on the schedule that works for both NASCAR and IndyCar."

If IndyCar does go to Kansas in May, it would add to an already jam-packed month. Teams would go straight from the Indianapolis 500 open test on May 4 and 5 to Kansas before returning to Indianapolis Motor Speedway for the Sonsio Grand Prix on May 15. That would lead straight into the two weeks of Indy 500 practice and qualifying and the Indy 500 (May 30) before the series races on the streets of Detroit (June 6) and World Wide Technology Raceway (June 13).

The grind of May and early June already drew the ire of some in the paddock , and another race could make that worse. At the same time, the series had success – both attendance-wise and via televison viewership – partnering with NASCAR in 2026, and it may not be a bad idea to do so twice in 2027.

IndyCar has kept its schedule at 17 races or fewer in recent years, with 2026 being the exception. (Washington, D.C.'s Freedom 250 Grand Prix was a late addition in January after President Donald Trump signed an executive order to have the race.) Mark Miles, the CEO and president of IndyCar parent company Penske Entertainment, said going beyond 17 races has been a discussion between him and Penske Entertainment chairman Roger Penske.

"We need to make sure that it makes economic sense for the series and for the teams," Miles said. "The team owners, it costs them to race. So we got to bring some more revenue in. But when things are done in an orchestrated way, I think there's potential."

For now, IndyCar is just seeing how its car would run on Kansas Speedway's progressive banking oval. If O'Ward and Power's test goes well, it could lead to another late addition to the calendar. The track will not be open to the public for the test.

articles.title: Las Vegas Grand Prix: George Russell fastest in second practice after rain
articles.summary: Mercedes' George Russell topped a second practice session at the Las Vegas Grand Prix run on a wet but slowly drying track.
articles.body:
Mercedes driver George Russell topped a second practice session at the Las Vegas Grand Prix run on a wet but slowly drying track.

Russell, competing with Red Bull's Max Verstappen for second in the championship in the final three races of the year, set his time right at the end of the session.

The same applied to Alpine's Pierre Gasly, who went second, 0.071 seconds behind Russell, with a lap even later the Briton's.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, the main pace-setter throughout the session, was third fastest ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar.

The Frenchman had a faster lap ruined when he was blocked by Haas' Oliver Bearman at the end of the Strip.

Russell said: "We know in the wet it is different every lap, every session, realistically we were not the fastest today.

"McLaren looked exceptionally fast. Charles looked very fast at points, we just got the lap in when the track was at its driest and Norris didn't run.

"We have some things to understand because Kimi and I were very competitive in the wet last week and both of us were off the pace."

Hadjar added: "It was good fun but I don't think it's very useful for tomorrow. Just shaking down the car."

McLaren's Oscar Piastri was fifth, ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and the second McLaren of Lando Norris, who was fastest in the wettest early part of the session.

New world champion Kimi Antonelli was eighth fastest, ahead of Alpine's Franco Colapinto and Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso.

F1 bosses close to V8 engines deal from 2030

The art of protection - inside an F1 helmet factory

Verstappen did not run until late in the session but was complaining about a problem with his engine.

Perhaps surprisingly given the conditions, the session was incident-free, although it was stopped briefly in the closing stages to recover a plastic bag that had blown on to the circuit.

Williams driver Alex Albon said: "I'm always surprised when I see no crashes. Trickiest track of the year, lowest grip of the year, these cars and a wet track is a lot of sliding."

The forecast is for dry weather for the rest of the weekend and the teams' focus will be on understanding the tyres, with warm-up so difficult in the cold conditions and with low loads going through the tyres.

This issue is exacerbated this year with the new 'straight-line mode', in which the wings open to reduce drag on the straights to aid energy recovery.

Russell said: "It's always a challenge here in Vegas but the added challenge this year with the nature of the cars, the SM zones everywhere, you're not putting any vertical load in the tyres so they are getting substantially cooler in the straight than in the previous years and they were already pretty cool."

In the first practice session, no driver completed a timed lap because the track was extremely wet and teams preferred to save their limited allocation of wet-weather tyres.

Hamilton said: "It wasn't a great day just sitting around waiting. You can't really test much in those conditions. And everything you learn from today you have to forget because tomorrow is supposed to be dry, so we kind of start from tomorrow.

"Everyone is (going in blind). No-one has put the slicks on, so we will have to react quickly. Hopefully, it's not bad and we are there or thereabouts."

Live commentary on BBC Radio 5 Live and 5 Sports Extra; live text updates on BBC Sport website and app

Piastri will have a 10-place grid penalty for exceeding his engine-part allowance this season.

The new internal combustion engine the Australian needs as a result of a failure at the Mexico City Grand Prix two races ago is his fifth of the season - only four are permitted.

Piastri and team-mate Norris will also use the latest turbo Mercedes have produced under F1's engine upgrade scheme but that comes penalty-free.

That is not the case for Williams' Carlos Sainz, who will take the new turbo but it is his fifth of the season, so he also has a 10-place penalty which team-mate Alex Albon avoids despite also fitting the new turbo.

At the factory team, only Antonelli will use the new turbo. The team decided it was not worth Russell having it as it would have given him a 15-place grid penalty.

The turbo provides only a small performance upgrade and is more aimed at expanding the engine's useability for the 2027 season.

Bearman also has a grid penalty for engine changes and is set to start from the back of the grid.

articles.title: Alonso entra en el 'top-ten', con Russell en cabeza
articles.standfirst: La pista mojada condicionó los libres 2 en Las Vegas y Sainz tuvo un problema en el motor.
articles.summary: La pista mojada condicionó los libres 2 en Las Vegas y Sainz tuvo un problema en el motor.
articles.body: George Russell ha logrado el mejor tiempo de los libres 2 en Las Vegas con una diferencia mínima sobre Pierre Gasly y su Alpine, en una fase final en la que el asfalto se secaba y los tiempos iban mejorando. Leclerc había sido en mejor en las condiciones más complicadas y se vio relegado el tercero en los instante finales de una sesión que no va a servir para casi nada, pues la lluvia no debería volver en todo el fin de semana. Fernando Alonso, con una ronda final muy interesante, logró ascender al 10º, justo por delante de Lance Stroll, en el que es el mejor viernes de Aston Martin de toda la temporada. Las condiciones de pista deslizante, donde la potencia cuenta poco o nada, permitieron a los de Silverstone brillar gracias a sus chasis, pero no parece que puedan repetirlo el resto del fin de semana en seco. Carlos Sainz, por su parte, estaba cerca de los diez mejores cuando un problema en su motor le obligó a regresar a boxes y ya no pudo volver a la pelea. Ya tiene 5 posiciones de penalización en la parrilla del domingo por cambiar el turbo, pero podría ser algo peor. Con sólo 5 minutos de sesión disputados, Alonso sufrió una salida de pista, en la que daño de forma ligera el morro de su AMR26, aunque pudo regresar sin problemas al box para solucionar los desperfectos. Apenas se le colocó un poco de cinta adhesiva y el español regresó a la pista. Fernando regresó casi de inmediato con las gomas de lluvia extrema y se metió octavo, justo por delante de Carlos Sainz, antes de cambiar a los intermedios de lluvia que pedía la pista a falta de media hora para el final. articles.title: Las Vegas GP: George Russell tops practice for Mercedes as rain limits running on first day of track action
articles.summary: George Russell topped second practice from Pierre Gasly after there was very little running in first practice on a wet first day of track action; watch the Las Vegas GP on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday
articles.body:
After no timed laps were completed in first practice due to heavy rain falling throughout, the weather relented to allow plenty of running during the second session, albeit on a damp, slowly drying circuit that prevented the use of slick tyres.

The best lap times came at the end of the session, which took place on Thursday night in Las Vegas, when Russell pipped Gasly by 0.071s, with Ferrari's Charles Leclerc three tenths off the pace in third.

"Realistically we were not the fastest today. McLaren looked exceptionally fast. Charles looked very fast at points, we just got the lap in when the track was at its driest and Norris didn't run," said Russell.

"We have got some things to understand. We were very competitive in the wet last week [in Brazil] and both Kimi and I were off the pace."

Leclerc and McLaren's Lando Norris, who won last time out in Brazil, had traded the fastest times for most of the session in the wetter conditions.

Norris ended up seventh, behind Red Bull's Isack Hadjar, his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, but the times are likely to matter very little given qualifying and the race are expected to take place in dry conditions.

The schedule in Las Vegas runs a day earlier than a traditional F1 weekend, but the time difference means qualifying will take place at 4am on Saturday morning for UK viewers, with the race following at the same time on Sunday.

Remarkably, there were few incidents and the only red flag across the whole day was for a plastic bag blowing on to the circuit at the high-speed final corner in second practice.

New F1 world champion Kimi Antonelli was eighth fastest but will serve a five-place grid penalty after exceeding his internal combustion engine allocation for a second time this season.

Piastri, Williams' Carlos Sainz and Aston Martin's Lance Stroll have 10-place grid penalties for going over various power unit elements, while Haas' Oliver Bearman will start at the back.

Max Verstappen spent most of the day in the garage and completed only 10 laps in total as he finished second practice in 13th.

Verstappen, who is on a run of eight consecutive podiums, felt he had "no power" from the engine on the laps he completed and insisted "it was not normal" despite his engineer suggesting the issue was related to the power unit needing to warm up in the cold condtions.

McLaren and Mercedes have brought upgrades this weekend but the rain on Thursday meant it was virtually impossible to tell whether they made any impact. McLaren revealed they did not even run the new floor parts in the two practice sessions.

Final practice, which gets under way at 12.30am on Saturday for UK viewers, is set to be very busy as the drivers will attempt to get plenty of dry laps in before qualifying.

articles.title: La F1 y Nike se unen en una alianza histórica
articles.standfirst: La firma de Oregón y el Gran Circo firman una colaboración global en el mundo del deporte
articles.summary: La firma de Oregón y el Gran Circo firman una colaboración global en el mundo del deporte
articles.body: No es la primera vez que Nike se asoma a la F1, pues todo el mundo recuerda las botas de MIchael Schumacher con el 'swoosh' en los inicios de este siglo, pero lo que llega ahora es un acuerdo global y a largo plazo con uno de los deportes de mayor proyección. No se han dado cifras, pero inicialmente podrían estar por encima de los 100 millones de dólares anuales para este nuevo patrocinio. La Fórmula 1 ha anunciado este jueves una asociación a largo plazo con Nike, en lo que supone la unión de dos de las marcas más influyentes del mundo del deporte. "Nike aportará una nueva energía a la máxima categoría del automovilismo a través de colecciones centradas en el estilo, el rendimiento y el estilo de vida, que incluirán calzado, ropa y accesorios, además de innovaciones técnicas y experiencias durante los fines de semana de carreras", dice el comunicado oficial. A partir de 2027, Nike se une a la Fórmula 1 como socio oficial y se convierte en "el proveedor oficial de ropa y uniformes de la categoría, creando equipaciones, como la marca compartida que lucirá el personal en los eventos de F1", según se informa. Nike equipará a la F1 en los siguientes apartados: - Ropa y uniformes para el personal de F1 en todos los Grandes Premios. - Colecciones de ropa, zapatillas y accesorios para aficionados. - Colaboración con la F1 Academy para desarrollar prendas de alto rendimiento. - Activaciones y experiencias durante los fines de semana de los Grandes Premios de la F1.

articles.title: Las Vegas GP: Kimi Antonelli to serve grid penalty along with Oscar Piastri, Carlos Sainz, Lance Stroll, Oliver Bearman
articles.summary: New Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli will serve a five-place grid penalty for the Las Vegas Grand Prix; watch the Las Vegas GP on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday
articles.body:
New Formula 1 world champion Antonelli took his sixth internal combustion engine (ICE) of the season during Thursday's opening practice sessions in Las Vegas, breaching the limit of four across the year for the second time.

Given the penalty for a second breach is five rather than 10 grid places, the Mercedes driver will start no higher than sixth in the race, which begins on Sunday morning at 4am UK time (build-up from 2.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 .

Antonelli started from the back of the grid at the Italian Grand Prix for exceeding the limit on several power unit elements, including his ICE, but remarkably won his home race in Monza.

Mercedes have also fitted Antonelli with an upgraded turbocharger that they have brought to the event, but the Italian is not incurring a penalty for that as it is within his allowance of four for the season.

In June, Mercedes were granted one chance to upgrade their power unit this season after being found to be between two and four per cent behind the best-performing internal combustion engine - which was unexpectedly judged to be Red Bull's - by the FIA in the year's first ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) assessment window.

That ADUO upgrade, which Mercedes have focused on their power unit's turbo, is being used by seven of the eight Mercedes-powered cars on the grid, with Antonelli's team-mate George Russell the exception.

Russell has already used five turbos, one more than is permitted, due to unreliability earlier in the year, and a sixth would trigger a further five-place grid penalty.

The Briton, who dropped five places on the Sao Paulo Grand Prix grid due to an engine change, is in a five-way battle to finish runner-up to Antonelli in the standings with three races to go.

Who else has grid penalties for the Las Vegas GP?

McLaren's Oscar Piastri will serve a 10-place grid penalty as he has exceeded his ICE limit for the first time this season.

Williams' Carlos Sainz also has a 10-place grid penalty for exceeding the turbocharger limit, and Aston Martin's Lance Stroll has the same penalty for a new energy store and control electronics.

Oliver Bearman, who says he is "disappointed" to not have a Haas contract signed for 2027 , has changed several power unit elements and will start at the back of the grid.

The long straights in Las Vegas means overtaking is relatively easy, so, in theory, it is a good track to take a grid penalty.

Russell topped a rain-affected second practice on Thursday night in Las Vegas after the weather had prevented any lap times from being set in the opening session.

The opening day of track action provided few clues of how the remainder of the weekend is likely to play out, with both qualifying and the race expected to take place in dry conditions.

articles.summary: Marc Márquez podría cerrar el Mundial consiguiendo su 10ª corona
articles.body: Penúltimo fin de semana antes de finalizar la temporada 2026 y un Gran Premio de Portugal que puede coronar, no sólo a uno, sino a dos pilotos, pues Manu González también tiene bola de partido en Portimao. Marc Márquez necesita un total de 3 puntos más sobre Jorge Martín para poder ganar el Mundial de MotoGP 2026, lo cual podría ser el mismo sábado, de acabar la Sprint con una diferencia de 63 puntos sobre el '89' en la clasificación general y quedar un total de 62 puntos. Del mismo modo, aunque sea muy difícil, Marco Bezzecchi aún tiene opciones matemáticas de llevarse el Mundial pues, la diferencia de puntos con el '93' son precisamente los que quedan en juego, 74, y tan sólo les separa una victoria: 7 de Marc frente a las 6 de Marco. No obstante, además de tenerlo muy complicado, el de Ducati recupera a uno de sus mayores aliados, pues Álex Márquez, su hermano, regresa a la acción este fin de semana, tras haberse perdido el Gran Premio de Qatar. Mientras, 'Pecco' Bagnaia, será baja, pues tras su caída en la Sprint del Gran Premio de Qatar, tuvo que pasar por quirófano para operarse del 5º metatarso de su pie derecho. Al '63' le sustituirá Iker Lecuona, sumando otro español más a la 'squadra' italiana. En la categoría pequeña, y con el Mundial ya decidido desde hace varias carreras, Quiles tratará de sumar otra victoria más, dado que ya no puede ni superar ni alcanzar las 14 de David Alonso. articles.title: The art of protection - inside a Formula 1 helmet factory
articles.summary: Inside the extraordinary world of Formula 1 helmets, where precision engineering, personal expression and life-saving technology join forces.
articles.body:
As soft, instrumental opera music plays in the background of a precise temperature-controlled room in northern Italy, Thomaso is using a children's toy ball and hairdryer to perform his meticulous work.

Hugely focused, in a crisp white coat, he moulds a precious sticky black material over and over again for up to six hours.

One day, his fastidiousness may save the life of one of the best athletes in the world.

The room Thomaso works in is called "the magic shop". Its motto? 'One man, one shell.'

Much of what happens inside is top secret. What we can say is the black material Thomaso is working with is a blend of carbon fibre that has to be stored at exactly -16°C. He moulds it into a secret form, layer by layer, after which the entire unit is baked in a vacuum bag at a set pressure at 120C for three-and-a-half hours.

The handmade products he is working on are personally chosen by their clients - for their safety features, as well as comfort, practicality and look.

Thomaso's colleague Sven travels the world between February and December to keep those clients happy. A different country almost every week, with a reliable weather forecast almost as important as a large allowance of hand luggage.

Together with 32 colleagues, Thomaso and Sven work for one of the four leading manufacturers of F1 helmets.

They produce sophisticated engineering masterpieces, and works of art.

"Our philosophy is to make the best product for the best drivers," says chief executive Alberto Dall'Oglio.

From leather caps to life-saving technology

In the early days of grand prix racing, protection was rudimentary. Drivers often wore little more than leather flying caps, goggles and - eventually - relatively basic open-face helmets.

Safety standards were inconsistent, materials primitive and the consequences of an accident frequently devastating.

According to the official F1 website, Giuseppe Farina - the first winner of an F1 race and first world champion - competed wearing nothing more than "his trusty cloth cap, two pairs of goggles (he wore the spare pair round his neck), cotton dungarees, leather boots and leather gloves".

The arrival of the full-face helmet in the late 1960s marked a defining moment. Bell introduced its pioneering Star model in 1966, and Dan Gurney became the first driver to race in a full-face helmet in 1968. The face - previously exposed to flying debris, fire and impact - finally had meaningful protection.

Progress was painfully slow, and motorsport's darkest moments repeatedly exposed the limitations of the technology.

In 1976, Niki Lauda 's Ferrari erupted into flames at the Nurburgring. His helmet came loose, leaving his head exposed to the fire. He survived, but suffered severe burns and lifelong injuries. The accident became a defining lesson in the importance of helmet retention, fire resistance and the protection of the driver's entire head.

The tragic deaths of Roland Ratzenberger and Ayrton Senna at Imola in 1994, followed by Jules Bianchi's fatal accident at Suzuka in 2014, demonstrated even increasingly sophisticated helmets could not eliminate every danger.

Ratzenberger suffered a fatal basilar skull fracture; Senna succumbed to multiple fractures of the skull base, after a strut from the suspension pierced his helmet.

Bianchi's accident exposed the vulnerability of drivers' heads to heavy external impacts. Helmets are only one part of a much wider safety system, which now includes stronger survival cells, the Hans device and the halo.

In 2004, the FIA introduced its new helmet safety standard, requiring advanced carbon-fibre construction to deliver greater strength, improved impact protection and reduced weight for F1 drivers.

At Bahrain's Sakhir circuit in 2020, Romain Grosjean's Haas split apart against the barriers and burst into flames. After 28 seconds trapped in the wreckage, he emerged with burns to his hands and ankles. His Bell helmet, fire-resistant equipment and the halo were instrumental in saving his life - a powerful testament to decades of safety innovation and engineering.

"Today's helmets are withstanding up to 30 seconds at 700, even 800, degrees," says Dall'Oglio. "Then they have to self-extinguish within 15 seconds."

Dall'Oglio is the CEO of Schuberth Performance, Thomaso an engineer and Sven a racing service technician, working trackside at more than 400 grands prix, preparing helmets and visors for rain, sun or floodlights.

Needing to avoid any impact on the helmets, he must carry them - sometimes five or six at a time - to races.

German engineering, Italian manufacturing

Schuberth, a German firm, has a long history in head protection. Founded in 1922, the company began making industrial products before moving into helmet linings in the late 1920s, then mining and motorcycle helmets in the 1950s.

With its HQ in Magdeburg and F1 helmet production in Schio, northern Italy, it produces special helmets for military forces - made of Kevlar, and some of a similar carbon - in the same factory as the F1 helmets.

Its motorsport credentials grew considerably around the turn of the millennium.

Following Michael Schumacher's British Grand Prix accident in 1999, Schuberth developed a new generation of racing helmets, subsequently worn by Schumacher and other leading drivers.

Of the current drivers, four-time world champion Max Verstappen is the most prominent to wear a Schuberth helmet. He is joined by Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar, Cadillac's Sergio Perez, Audi's Nico Hulkenberg and Arvid Lindblad at Racing Bulls.

Dall'Oglio's team hand-makes about 250 helmets a year.

'We work hard to remove 20g of weight... then a driver can add decoration of 80g'

An F1 helmet is a remarkable marriage of science and aesthetics.

Constructed using advanced composite materials, including carbon fibre, it must be exceptionally strong while remaining light enough to minimise strain on a driver's neck.

Visors, ventilation systems, fire-resistant linings, communication equipment, a straw-like drinks system and carefully designed retention mechanisms all contribute to its performance.

Today, F1 helmets must withstand a 225g metal projectile fired at 155mph, a 790C flame and substantial impact and crushing tests. It is engineering with virtually no margin for compromise.

Schuberth works closely with motorsport governing body the FIA.

Dall'Oglio says: "There's a constant exchange of information. We are repeating tests on a regular basis. We are also working on the future regulation of the helmets.

"With the tiniest structural or superficial defect, the carbon shell cannot be used. This could be a lamination, a cooking or a tool problem. So it could be over 1,000 euros (£850) in material, and all those hours of work will have become obsolete."

Arai, Bell and Stilo are the three other leading manufacturers of F1 helmets.

Dall'Oglio says: "We all have the same issues, and in the end, we are protecting drivers. So, the responsibility is heavy for all of us.

"It's the fun part to work with the drivers, but it's also a high responsibility."

When I visit, production is paused and the team cluster to solve a problem. Thankfully this happens very rarely - and the majority of helmet shells are taken to the next station: a water-jet cutting system with a "needle" of water slicing through the rock-hard carbon.

It's 4,000 bars of pressure, like a knife through warm butter, to create the narrow visor opening, six centimetres at its highest point.

"It is genius, because you don't use mechanical force on to the helmet," explains Dall'Oglio.

The cut shell is then taken to what they call "the jigsaw" - the assembly point.

Dall'Oglio says: "The outer shell is created of nearly 100 pieces. Now we add another 100 pieces, depending on the type of aerodynamics parts we need to add on. In total, we can say a couple of hundred pieces make a helmet."

Once assembled, the helmet is taken to the driver's designer.

A helmet can be a driver's signature. From Senna's iconic Brazilian colours to Schumacher's Ferrari red, the designs are miniature works of art.

Combining intricate graphics, specialist paintwork and personal touches, each livery tells a story, celebrating a driver's heritage, family or defining moments.

But while fancy designs look fabulous, they can create headaches for the team in Schio.

"A helmet overall weighs about 1.4 kg, depending on the decoration, and aerodynamic specification," says Dall'Oglio.

"We try to work hard to remove like 20, 30 grams from the top-of-the-line helmets, and a driver then adds decoration of 80 or 70 grams. It's always a little bit of a negotiation with the driver and the painter, but in the end, it's their decision."

Dall'Oglio is proud of the company's relationship with Verstappen, who is very good at giving feedback to initiate improvements.

"We continue on cultivating it, of course, but it's like a happy marriage," he says.

The helmets produced by Dall'Oglio, his colleagues, and other firms are extraordinary pieces of design and engineering, but the greatest achievement will never be the paintwork, carbon-fibre finish or name emblazoned across the side.

Thomaso smiles, as he knows. It is the life they help save, and the driver who walks away.

articles.summary: MotoGP podría volver a tener un campeón el sábado
articles.body: Marc Márquez podría volver a reinar el Mundial de MotoGP, sellando su 10ª corona, 8ª en la categoría reina, este fin de semana en el Gran Premio de Portugal. Además, podrá hacerlo, si todas las cuentas acaban cuadrando, en la Sprint del sábado. Sin embargo, no sería el primero, pues hace 22 años, en 2002, Valentino Rossi consiguió su segundo Mundial de la categoría reina en el Gran Premio de Rio, con la 500cc. No obstante, para poder alcanzar el 10ª el sábado, en su segundo 'Match Ball', el '93' tendrá que hacer cuentas, aunque menos que en Qatar, donde también tuvo bola de partido aunque, en este caso, será más sencillo, pues con sumar 3 puntos más que Jorge Martín al acabar la Sprint, Marc será campeón. La situación actual es la siguiente: dos Grandes Premios restantes, Portugal y Valencia, con un total de 74 puntos en juego y una diferencia de 60 sobre Martín y 74 sobre Bezzecchi. Al acabar la Sprint de Portugal, quedarán un total de 62 puntos en juego, por lo que, de sumar esos tres puntos sobre Martín, y que la diferencia pasase de 60 a 63, Marc Márquez se proclamaría campeón del mundo de MotoGP. A pesar de tener justo la diferencia de puntos que quedan, 74, y de estar virtualmente fuera de la lucha, la realidad es que, matemáticamente, aún es posible que Bezzecchi gane el Mundial. El italiano cuenta con un total de 6 victorias, frente a las 7 de Marc Márquez. Por ello, de sumar los 74 puntos restantes y empatar con Marc a final de temporada, el '72' se proclamaría campeón del mundo por número de victorias. articles.standfirst: Niega una retirada tras ganar el título, se compara consigo mismo y más
articles.summary: Niega una retirada tras ganar el título, se compara consigo mismo y más
articles.body: En los últimos días, varios antiguos competidores de MotoGP, como Marco Melandri o Stefan Bradl, que ahora ejercen como comentaristas, deslizaban la idea de que Marc Márquez estaría pensando en retirarse cuando ate su décimo título, es decir, a la conclusión de la presente temporada. Los dos aludían a "comentarios en el 'paddock'" para argumentar tales palabras. El aludido fue cuestionado en Portimao para saber la realidad de tales supuestos pensamientos. "Por el momento, estoy concentrado al cien por cien en cerrar esto. Tengo dos años más de contrato con Ducati. Este año ha sido muy difícil, pero sigo siendo rápido. La prioridad es cerrar este campeonato y trabajar para el año que viene", proclamó. El ilerdense disfrutaba viendo unas imágenes de sí mismo con un rostro muy infantil en su debut en el Mundial de MotoGP, en 2008, en Portugal, aunque en Estoril. "Crecí físicamente tarde, por eso tengo esa cara. En pretemporada me lesioné y por eso debuté aquí. En increíble que después de 18 años esté luchando por mi décimo título. He tenido muchísimo éxito en más de la mitad de mi vida", reconocía. Porque el de Cervera mantiene la motivación. "Tengo 33 años y en 18 estuve en el Mundial. Aún tengo pasión, que depende de muchas cosas. La vida del deportista es corta y hay que sacar partido de todo lo que puedas", soltaba con Jorge Martín asintiendo. Claro que el del Ducati oficial reconocía que su eterna sonrisa se ha visto mucho menos en 2026 que en otros cursos. ¿Se debe a que ya no disfruta? Él lo matizaba. "Cuando tienes dificultades, disfrutas menos; con las lesiones, disfrutas menos. El año pasado disfruté más. Este año he trabajado más que el pasado. Cuando tienes un objetivo, eso cubre cosas como un campeonato, con lo que disfrutas ganando", exponía. El mayor de los Márquez fue requerido a valorarse a sí mismo. Para empezar, cuál considera que es el Marc más rápido. "Fue el de 2013, 2014 o 2019", decía. "Si me tengo que quedar con uno, el de 2019, gané o hice segundo en todas las carreras menos Austin, donde me caí liderando por cuatro segundos", añadió. Con lo segundo no tuvo dudas. Fue al replicar si esta versión es la mejor suya. "El mejor Marc es el de ahora, al cien por cien. Me hubiera gustado tener esta mentalidad antes, pero igual con esta mentalidad no habría hecho algunas cosas", concluyó.

articles.title: F1 bosses close to V8 turbo hybrid engines deal from 2030
articles.summary: Formula 1 bosses are close to a deal that will see V8 turbo hybrid engines replace the current controversial engines in 2030.
articles.body:
Formula 1 bosses are close to a deal that will see V8 turbo hybrid engines replace the current controversial engines in 2030.

McLaren chief executive officer Zak Brown said an "agreement in principle" had been reached by engine manufacturers and F1 bosses on the new rules.

These will be for a 2.1-litre V8 turbo engine with a smaller electrical element than this year, as first revealed by BBC Sport last month.

Some details remain to be resolved but the main core of the rules has been agreed.

The electrical element will be for a maximum power output of 200kW - compared with 350kW this year.

But only half of that will be available at all times, with the remaining half used only for an overtake mode.

A key element of the rules will be to remove the issue of energy starvation that has been criticised by the drivers this year for taking away "pure" racing.

But the overall power output of the engines will be similar to now.

The combustion engine will have about 780bhp, while 200kW is 270bhp.

That means a total power output of 1,050bhp in overtake mode or just over 900bhp in standard running.

Brown said: "Everyone is very, very excited. Now it's about kind of dotting the i's and crossing the t's.

"I'm excited for the new engines, I think everyone will be, the power units. But there's a lot more also going on to continue to evolve the sport. So, between the FIA and Formula 1, they're doing a great job."

Russell fastest in Las Vegas practice after rain

How to follow Las Vegas Grand Prix on the BBC

Alpine executive director Flavio Briatore said: "We have the agreement, basically. It's not signed, but it looks like everybody's agreed to 2030 V8s, and I'm very happy.

"It's the right way to go. We need an engine with a lot of noise, and a simple engine, and we need to be racing with that."

The ruleset amounts to a compromise reached by manufacturers after FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem initially pushed for a naturally aspirated engine without turbo or electrical components.

But these were required to reduce overall fuel consumption, and therefore weight at the start of races.

That means Ben Sulayem's desire for a return to the loud volumes of the previous V8 era from 2006 to 2013 will not be achieved. The engines are expected to sound similar to now.

This was important because a significant increase in engine noise would have put at threat some races in city centres that are commercially important to F1, such as Miami and Las Vegas.

The 2.1-litre capacity has been arrived at because it amounts to adding to two cylinders to the current 1.6-litre V6 blocks, with the aim of reducing development costs.

Cars are expected to start races with about 110-120kg of fuel, up from about 100kg now. A total weight limit of 150kg for the power-units will be imposed, down by about 30kg from the current engines.

There will be a fuel energy flow limit to keep the power of the combustion engine under control, and a budget cap figure for engines set at $190m (£145m) per year.

As part of negotiations, General Motors, backers of the Cadillac team, will delay the production of its new engine until 2030. It had been scheduled for 2029.

In return, GM will lose its voting rights on current engine rules and be classified as a new manufacturer from 2030.

The team will continue to use Ferrari customer engines through 2029.

Cadillac F1 chief executive officer Dan Towriss said: "For a period of time, we were working on both. So, they've already got a V6 base to build off of, and working towards the V8.

"There are a number of designs that are in motion now, and so there's a lot of good foundation for what we're trying to build and the direction we're headed in."

articles.summary: Estaba cerca de entrar con los 10 mejores, cuando llegó un problema en su unidad de potencia en los libres 2
articles.body: Carlos Sainz estaba en uno de sus escenarios preferidos, con frío, poco agarre y condiciones muy delicadas, pero cerca de meterse entre los 10 mejores puestos de los libres 2 en Las Vegas. Tras su primer stint le llamaron a boxes y ya no pudo regresar al asfalto. Luego se confirmó que va a ser penalizado con 10 puestos en la parrilla del domingo, por montar un nuevo turbo en el motor Mercedes de su Williams FW-48. "Ha sido un viernes un tanto extraño aquí en Las Vegas debido a la lluvia. La primera sesión de entrenamientos libres (FP1) se vio frustrada por el agua. En la segunda (FP2)... logramos dar algunas vueltas con neumáticos intermedios antes de que surgiera un pequeño problema en la unidad de potencia que me obligó a detenerme a mitad de la sesión", resumía en su análisis para Williams. "Pero esa fue una tanda bastante importante para mí con los neumáticos intermedios ( de lluvia), ya que habíamos tenido algunos problemas con ellos en Brasil. Quería asegurarme de tener un buen ritmo y me alegró mucho comprobar que era realmente competitivo con ese compuesto. Así que, bueno, ese es el aspecto positivo de hoy. Mañana y el domingo el tiempo será seco, por lo que el escenario será totalmente distinto al de hoy. Tendremos que aprenderlo todo durante la tercera sesión de entrenamientos libres, así que será muy interesante", analizaba el piloto madrileño.

articles.title: Lando Norris: McLaren chief Zak Brown says he wouldn't trade 2025 world champion for any other driver on F1 grid
articles.summary: Lando Norris has claimed three race victories this season despite McLaren having failed to maintain the level that had brought them successive constructors' titles; watch the Las Vegas GP on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday
articles.body:
Norris last year claimed McLaren's first Drivers' Championship since 2008 but has arguably performed even more impressively this season despite sitting sixth in the standings with three races remaining.

Having come out on top last year in a tight battle with his team-mate Oscar Piastri and Red Bull's Max Verstappen, Norris has dominated the Australian this season, with his third grand prix victory of the season last time out in Brazil extending the gap between them to 94 points.

Asked by Sky Sports F1 at this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix about Norris' level of performance, Brown said: "I think he's never driven better. He's driving with a lot of confidence.

"I think the biggest thing I've noticed with Lando this year, when we have a bad session, how quickly he recovers, and he leads himself and the team forward, so I do think he's driving with another year's experience.

"I think Brazil was an amazing drive. Ranking drivers is always difficult. What I would say is I wouldn't want to trade him for anyone else on the grid."

'Verstappen as good as anyone we've ever seen in F1'

Despite his position on Norris, Brown offered high praise to Verstappen during the same press conference.

The four-time world champion was briefly linked to McLaren this summer before committing his future to Red Bull with a new long-term deal.

Verstappen almost overturned a huge deficit to win last year's championship, and has produced another spectacular turnaround this season to surge up to second in the standings behind Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli, who was crowned champion earlier in November.

"He's an unbelievable talent," Brown said of Verstappen. "He's as good as anyone I think we've ever seen in Formula 1, never really makes mistakes, tricky conditions seem to play his way."

Verstappen finished second to Norris in Brazil earlier in November despite starting from the back row of the grid after receiving a penalty for taking a new engine.

Brown continued: "And so look at Brazil again. There are a lot of drivers, if they take a penalty or they start at the back, you can go, 'we don't have to worry about them today'.

"But I think when it's Max Verstappen, as long as he's on the racetrack, you need to worry about him.

"So he's just an awesome, awesome driver. It's great to watch him race, and I also like that on his weekends off he still goes in races, so he's a proper racer, and I think he's a talent unlike many we've seen before."

'Piastri is looking forward to next season'

While Norris has impressed, Piastri has struggled to maintain the high standards he set in 2025 by building a considerable lead in the title battle before wilting over the final third of the season.

The Australian has struggled, at least compared to Norris, with the vastly different style of the all-new cars introduced for the 2026 season following a major regulation change.

McLaren are not the only team where there has been a shift in driver performance, with champion Antonelli surprisingly outperforming George Russell, and Lewis Hamilton faring much better against Charles Leclerc at Ferrari than he had done the previous year.

Brown said: "The cars have been different to drive this year. Some of the driver line-ups have been mixed up from what we saw last year.

"Some drivers, these cars fit their style more than others. Oscar is very brave, especially in the high-speed corners.

"In today's racecars, some corners you might take flat, you have to conserve some battery, so it doesn't allow you to be at the limit in some of the corners he excels at.

"He's much improved and feels much more confident. We are confident. We know how good he is. He will get on top of it shortly."

Pushed on whether Norris has adapted better to the new cars, Brown added: "Lando is as naturally talented as they get. Some drivers take to this stuff quicker than others.

"Oscar's a very good student of data and I have no doubt he will be very strong in the final three races and is looking forward to next season."

articles.standfirst: Aston Martin concluye un viernes aceptable y Russell busca el 2º puesto en el Mundial
articles.summary: Aston Martin concluye un viernes aceptable y Russell busca el 2º puesto en el Mundial
articles.body: Primer día del Gran Premio de Las Vegas pasado por agua. El Mundial de F1 encara su último triplete del año y arranca en Las Vegas con el antepenúltimo fin de semana antes de concluir la temporada 2026, con muchas vistas puestas ya en 2027, pero varias incógnitas aún por resolver. Con unos Libres 1 sin acción prácticamente en pista debido a la lluvia, arrancaron a las 05:00 hora peninsular, la segunda sesión del viernes en la que Russell se impuso, seguido de Pierre Gasly y Leclerc, con un tiempo de 1.47.272 y neumáticos intermedios, dando a ver que está dispuesto a luchar por cerrar el círculo perfecto de Mercedes este año, consiguiendo la segunda posición del Mundial y sumarlo al título de Antonelli y de Constructores. Mientras tanto, Fernando Alonso volvió a aprovechar la oportunidad que le dio la meteorología y logró firmar un 10º puesto en la segunda sesión del viernes, a pesar del susto inicial que dejó tocado su morro. A eso, se le añade la 11ª posición de su compañero de equipo, Lance Stroll, cerrando así uno de los mejores días de Aston Martin en lo que llevan de temporada. Por otro lado, la cruz del viernes se la llevó Carlos Sainz. El de Williams no pudo acabar la sesión debido a un fallo en su motor, dejándole a más de 4 segundos del líder, Russell, y lo que le acarreará una sanción de cara a la carrera del domingo. Una vez sentenciado el Mundial de Pilotos y el de Constructores, siguen habiendo dos temas importantes a tener en cuenta, y cuyos actores se han convertido en protagonistas. Por un lado, la segunda posición del Mundial entre Russell, Hamilton, Norris, Verstappen y Leclerc, separados por tan sólo 33 puntos y con una lucha abierta, pues los cinco demuestran cada fin de semana y cada sesión tener oportunidad de conseguirlo. No obstante, hoy les tocó sufrir precisamente a los dos últimos ganadores de Grandes Premios: Norris y Verstappen, quienes quedaron 7º y 13º consecutivamente a más de un segundo el británico y casi tres el neerlandés. Además, estos dos últimos mencionados siguen luchando por dar la mejor posición posible a sus equipos en el Mundial de Constructores, pues McLaren y Red Bull buscan cerrar el año en la tercera posición y, por el momento, tan sólo 17 puntos les separan. Como es habitual, el Gran Premio de Las Vegas de Fórmula 1 2026 se podrá ver en directo por televisión a través de DAZN F1 y en Movistar+. También tienes la opción de seguir todo lo que suceda en la carrera en Las Vegas a través de los directos de MARCA.com y la transmisión de la carrera en Radio MARCA.
